title: French Bistro Tarragon-Mustard Velouté
description: A pale roux, tarragon and a touch of freshly bloomed mustard make a light French-style sauce for chicken or fish.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Use plain homemade or unsalted carton broth at about 35 mg sodium per cup, with household-approved ingredients.

ingredients.name: table salt
ingredients.note: Fine table salt, about 590 mg sodium per 1/4 teaspoon. Low-sodium batch: use 1/16 tsp total.

steps.title: Make a pale roux
steps.text: Melt {bf} in the skillet and whisk in {fl} over medium-low heat for 90 seconds. Keep the paste pale.

steps.title: Infuse the tarragon
steps.text: Gradually whisk in {ch}, then {tar} and {ms}. Simmer for 4–5 minutes until the sauce coats a spoon.

steps.title: Round out the sauce
steps.text: Whisk in {milk} and {salt}. Warm gently for 1 minute, then stir in {le} off the heat.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 cup. If short, loosen with a little hot sodium-free water. If over, return it to the pan and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve the sauce
steps.text: Spoon over tender cutlets or steamed white fish and let the tarragon sauce pool around the edges.

notes: Yield: 1 cup, or four 1/4-cup portions. Low-sodium option for the full batch: Use 1/16 tsp table salt in place of 1/4 tsp. Use the same final 1-cup yield and 1/4-cup serving. Make ahead: Make the sauce the day before and portion it before chilling. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: No. The milk sauce can separate or become grainy when frozen. Fridge reheat: Reheat a portion in a small pan, stirring to a brief boil and at least 165°F. Loosen with a splash of water if it tightens. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then use the fridge reheat method. Option A uses the listed seasonings. For a gentler Option B, skip the lemon and halve the mustard. For dairy-free velouté, use avocado oil and plain unsweetened oat milk in place of the butter and skim milk. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 33 kcal, 1.2 g protein, 2.5 g total carbohydrate, 2.1 g fat, 0.1 g fiber, 161 mg sodium. Low-sodium version per 1/4 cup: 33 kcal, 1.2 g protein, 2.5 g total carbohydrate, 2.1 g fat, 0.1 g fiber, 50 mg sodium. Figures cover the sauce alone. Sodium varies with brands.
